ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The small diagram on the left indicates that after a laser encounters a slanted mirror, it will change direction according to specular reflection; both sides of the mirror can reflect. The large diagram on the right is a rectangular grid, with three vertical dashed-line positions, labeled A, B, and C respectively at the bottom; there are two horizontal dashed-line positions, labeled E (upper row) and D (lower row) respectively on the right side. The laser enters horizontally to the right from the left along the upper E row. The mirror positions in the right diagram are: at A-E is a backslash mirror, at A-D is a backslash mirror, at B-E is a slash mirror, at B-D is a slash mirror, at C-E is a backslash mirror, and at C-D is a slash mirror. Reasoning: The laser enters to the right along the E row, first hits the backslash mirror at A-E, and its direction changes to downward; after reaching the backslash mirror at A-D, its direction changes to rightward; after reaching the slash mirror at B-D, its direction changes to upward; after reaching the slash mirror at B-E, its direction changes to rightward; after reaching the backslash mirror at C-E, its direction changes to downward; after reaching the slash mirror at C-D, its direction changes to leftward; when it again reaches the slash mirror at B-D, its direction changes to downward, and so it exits from the bottom in column B. Therefore the laser finally reaches the letter B.
